newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-B.Philp finds spice too hot to handle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-B.Philp finds spice too hot to handle.

text.p: Burns Philp & Co Ltd said on Monday it would sell its herb and spice businesses in North America and Europe and return its focus to producing yeast.
The Australian food ingredients group also announced the retirement of managing director Ian Clack, the man promoted three years ago to oversee the company's expansion into more exotic condiments.
Burns Philp announced a loss for the third quarter to March 31, 1997 and added that profits for the three months ended June 30, would be below the year-ago level but better than the third quarter.
Investors welcomed the surprise announcements, pushing Burns Philp shares up five percent or 11 cents to A$1.96.
"Its positive for Burns Philp," said a senior Sydney broker.

Burns Philp was under pressure from investors concerned that the group was on course for a fourth successive annual profit drop. Over 60 percent has being wiped off its share price value since January 1994.

The food group said it had made a third quarter net loss of A$23.4 million compared with a profit of A$7.1 million in the three months ended March 31, 1996. Net profit for the nine months fell to A$23.8 million from A$48.1 million a year ago.
The company said it was looking for a new managing director following Clack's retirement.

The sale of its spice and herb business is a retreat from the company's plans to expand in the food business after a massive restructing which was largely complete in May 1994 when it sold the BBC Hardware stores for A$460 million.

Burns Philp used the sale proceeds from BBC Hardware to fund an aggressive buying spree of food-related businesses including U.S. spice business Tone Brothers -- one of the operations put up for sale on Monday.
Tone Brothers has struggled with providing decent profit returns during its battle for market share in the United States with U.S. food group McCormick & Co.
